title: Agent Typewriter repository settings
description: Agent Typewriter settings for this repository. Workspace settings override these; these override user settings.

autoStart.description: Start watching automatically when a workspace opens.

include.description: Workspace-relative globs to watch. A pattern without a slash (like *.ts) matches the file name anywhere.

exclude.description: Workspace-relative globs to ignore. Exclude wins over include.

extensions.description: Only watch these file extensions (for example ["ts", "java", "md"]). Empty means any extension that passes include/exclude.

respectGitignore.description: Also skip paths git ignores (.gitignore files, .git/info/exclude, and your global excludes). Files git tracks are never skipped. Has no effect without git or outside a git repository.

profiles.markdownDescription: Named filter sets, for example `{ "docs": { "include": ["docs/**"], "extensions": ["md"] } }`. Profiles merge by name with those in `.agent-typewriter.json`. Switch with **Switch Filter Profile...**.

activeProfile.description: Name of the active filter profile. Its filters override the repository settings file and user settings; workspace settings still override it. Empty means no profile.

charsPerMinute.description: Base typing speed in characters per minute.

charsPerSecond.description: Deprecated: use charsPerMinute. Base typing speed in characters per second; applies times 60 where charsPerMinute is not set.

languageSpeeds.markdownDescription: Base typing speed per language, in characters per minute, keyed by VS Code language ID (for example `{ "markdown": 600, "json": 1200 }`). Language IDs are case-sensitive; find them in the language picker in the status bar. Languages not listed use `#agentTypewriter.charsPerMinute#`.

jitter.description: How uneven the typing rhythm is. 0 is perfectly even, 1 is very uneven.

catchUpFactor.description: Extra speed per queued change, so playback accelerates when the agent gets ahead. Speed = base x (1 + factor x queued), capped at maxSpeedup.

maxSpeedup.description: Upper bound on the automatic catch-up multiplier.

maxAnimatedChars.description: Changes that add more characters than this are applied instantly instead of typed (big generated files, formatter runs).

fileSwitchDelayMs.description: Pause when playback flips to a different file, so the switch reads like a person changing tabs.

smoothScroll.description: Scroll to the next edit in the same file, after a short pause, instead of jumping there. Edits already in view only move the caret.

scrollPauseMs.description: Pause before scrolling to the next edit in the same file, so the last lines typed can be read. Divided by the playback speed.

scrollLinesPerSecond.description: How fast the view scrolls to the next edit in the same file. A scroll takes at most one second at 1x; far edits jump most of the way first.

arrowNavigation.description: Walk the caret to the next edit with arrow keys (a line at a time, then by words) when it is close by and in view, instead of clicking there.

arrowKeysPerSecond.description: Arrow key presses per second when walking the caret to the next edit. Multiplied by the playback speed.

debounceMs.description: Writes to the same file within this window are merged into one change.

reorderWindowMs.markdownDescription: How long each change is held so changes reach the timeline in the order files were written, even when the file watcher reports them late. `"auto"` uses 2500 ms on Windows and 250 ms elsewhere. `0` adds changes as soon as they are read.

maxFileSizeKB.description: Files larger than this are ignored.

gitBaselines.description: For files git reports as tracked and unmodified, read the first change's before text from git instead of keeping a copy in memory. Needs the git command; turns itself off when git is not available. The watched repository is only read, never changed.

baselineBudgetMB.description: Memory budget for in-memory baselines (files not covered by git). Most recently modified files are covered first; a file without a baseline has its first change captured only as a baseline.

historyLimit.description: How many changes to keep in the buffer for replay. Oldest are dropped first.

persistHistory.description: Keep the recorded changes across window reloads and restarts, in VS Code's storage for this workspace (never in the workspace itself). Up to 64 MB of change text is kept, newest first. Turning this off deletes the saved history.

ignoreOwnSaves.description: Do not replay changes you saved from a VS Code editor yourself. Saves are matched by content: if something else writes the file right after your save, that write is still replayed. Turn off if your agent edits VS Code's editor buffers and then saves them.

viewColumn.description: Where the replay editor opens: in a column beside your current editor, or in the active column.

mirrorStatusRow.description: Show a row of playback controls and status above the first line of the replay editor. Turn off to keep it out of screen recordings. Hidden anyway when editor.codeLens is off.
